lines: A sailor's old scar splits open, years after it healed.
His gums are bleeding. His teeth are loose.
And he's not the only one. The ship's surgeon says this disease kills more British sailors than enemy guns.
So the surgeon, James Lind, picks twelve sick men and splits them into six pairs.
Each pair gets a different cure. Cider. Vinegar. Seawater.
And one pair gets two oranges and a lemon, every day.
Fruit? Against the deadliest killer at sea?
Six days later, the fruit runs out.
But one of those two men is already back on duty.
You see, think of the last time you cut yourself.
Your body sewed it shut with collagen, tiny ropes that hold your skin together.
And to tie those ropes, your body needs vitamin C. It can't make its own.
Months at sea with no fresh food, and the knots start slipping. Even the old ones.
Two oranges and a lemon did what medicine couldn't.
And the navy took forty-eight years to listen.
